rule_metadata.rule_name_english: Madd Munfasil (Separated Madd) & Madd Lazim (Compulsory Madd)
rule_metadata.description: Comprehensive rules covering the 4-to-5 count separated lengthening across two words and the mandatory 6-count compulsory lengthening caused by permanent sukoon or shaddah.

madd_munfasil.name: Madd Munfasil (Separated Permissible Madd)
madd_munfasil.definition: Occurs when a Madd letter appears at the very end of a word, and the succeeding Hamzah (ء) begins the immediately following word.
madd_munfasil.ruling: Extended for 4 to 5 counts according to the narration of Hafs 'an 'Asim (permissible to shorten to 2 counts in certain auxiliary transmission paths, but 4-5 is standard).
madd_munfasil.example: بِمَا أُنْزِلَ (Bima unzila), يَا أَيُّهَا (Ya ayyuha)

madd_lazim.name: Madd Lazim (Compulsory / Mandatory Madd)
madd_lazim.definition: Occurs when a Madd letter is followed by a permanent Sukoon (or Shaddah representing a doubled letter) within the **same word** or inside the disjointed letters (Al-Huroof al-Muqatta'ah) at the start of Surahs.
madd_lazim.ruling: Strictly and universally extended for exactly **6 counts** (Harakat) across all authentic schools of recitation.

sub_divisions.kalimi_thaqil: Mutawassaq / Kalimi Thaqil: Word-based heavy (Madd followed by Shaddah, e.g., الضَّالِّينَ).
sub_divisions.kalimi_khafif: Kalimi Khafif: Word-based light (Madd followed by Sukoon, e.g., آلْآنَ).
sub_divisions.harfi_thaqil: Harfi Thaqil: Letter-based heavy in disjointed letters (e.g., الم in Alif-Lam-Meem where Meem merges into Meem).
sub_divisions.harfi_khafif: Harfi Khafif: Letter-based light in disjointed letters (e.g., ن in Noon or ق in Qaf).

practical_examples.breakdown: Alif Madd at end of 'Bima' meets Hamzah at start of 'unzila'; extended 4-5 counts.
Alif Madd at end of 'Ya' meets Hamzah at start of 'ayyuha'.
Alif Madd followed by a Shaddah on the Lam inside the same word; extended strictly for 6 counts.
Madd letter followed by permanent Sukoon without merging.

assessment_bank.question: What defines Madd Munfasil (Separated Madd)?
options: A Madd letter at the end of a word followed by a Hamzah starting the next word
A Madd letter followed by Hamzah in the same word
A Madd letter followed by Sukoon
A Madd letter followed by Shaddah

assessment_bank.question: Why is Madd Munfasil called 'Munfasil' (Separated)?
options: Because the Madd letter and the Hamzah are separated across two different words
Because it occurs only at the start of verses

assessment_bank.question: How many counts are required for Madd Munfasil according to Hafs 'an 'Asim?
What defines Madd Lazim (Compulsory Madd)?
options: A Madd letter followed by a permanent Sukoon or Shaddah in the same word or letter
A Madd letter followed by a vowel

assessment_bank.question: How many counts must Madd Lazim be lengthened universally?
In the phrase 'بِمَا أُنْزِلَ', what Tajweed rule applies between the two words?
In the word 'الضَّالِّينَ', what Tajweed rule applies?
What does 'Thaqil' mean in Madd Lazim Kalimi Thaqil?
What does 'Khafif' mean in Madd Lazim?
options: Light (due to following Sukoon without Shaddah)

assessment_bank.question: Where does Madd Lazim Harfi occur?
options: Inside the disjointed letters (Al-Huroof al-Muqatta'ah) at the start of Surahs
At the very end of the Quran

assessment_bank.question: In 'يَا أَيُّهَا', how should the Alif in 'يَا' be lengthened?
Why is Madd Lazim called 'Lazim' (Compulsory)?
options: Because its 6-count duration is mandatory and binding across all recitation chains
Because it is only found in Surah Al-Baqarah

assessment_bank.question: In 'وَمَا أُمِرُوا', what rule governs the Alif meeting Hamzah across words?
Which of the following is a classic example of Madd Lazim Kalimi Khafif in the Quran?
What is the duration difference between Madd Munfasil and Madd Lazim?
options: Munfasil is 4-5 counts; Lazim is strictly 6 counts
Munfasil is 6 counts; Lazim is 2 counts

assessment_bank.question: In 'حَٓمْ ۝ عَسَقْ', what rule governs the letters with built-in Madd like 'م' and 'س'?
What happens if a reciter reads Madd Lazim with only 2 counts?
options: It is a major Tajweed error (Lahn Jali) violating the compulsory 6 counts

assessment_bank.question: In 'قٓ ۚ وَالْقُرْآنِ', how is the letter 'Qaf' (ق) at the start of Surah Qaf lengthened?
In 'المٓ', how is the letter 'Laam' (ل) lengthened?
options: 6 counts (Madd Lazim Harfi Thaqil because its spelling ends in Meem which merges into the next Meem)

assessment_bank.question: What is the structural difference between Madd Muttasil and Madd Munfasil?
options: Muttasil has the Hamzah in the same word (4-5 counts); Munfasil has the Hamzah at the start of the next word (4-5 counts)

assessment_bank.question: In 'قَالُوا آمَنَّا', what rule connects 'قَالُوا' and 'آمَنَّا'?
What symbol is typically placed over the Madd letter in Madd Munfasil in modern Mushafs?
Can Madd Munfasil be shortened to 2 counts under certain scholarly transmission routes (Turuq)?
options: Yes, in certain shorter recitation paths (Qasr al-Munfasil), but Hafs 'an 'Asim via Shatibiyyah standard is 4-5 counts

assessment_bank.question: In 'الْحَاقَّةُ', why is it classified as Madd Lazim Kalimi Thaqil?
options: Because the Alif Madd is followed by a doubled Qaf (Shaddah) in the same word
Because it is at the start of a Surah

assessment_bank.question: How should 'الْحَاقَّةُ' be recited?
options: Al-Haaqqah with 6 counts on the Alif before settling into the Qaf Shaddah

assessment_bank.question: What does 'Harfi' mean in Madd Lazim Harfi?
options: Pertaining to the isolated letters of the alphabet found at Surah openings

assessment_bank.question: Which disjointed letter at the start of Surahs has NO Madd at all?
Why does 'Alif' (أَلِفْ) in 'الم' have no Madd Lazim?
options: Because its middle letter is a Lam (vowelless), but it does not contain a central Madd letter in its three-letter spelling
Because it is at the end of the ayah

assessment_bank.question: In 'طٰهٰ', how are the letters Ta and Ha lengthened?
In 'كهيعص', which letters receive the full 6-count Madd Lazim?
What is the exact counting rhythm for a 6-count Madd Lazim?
options: A steady, unhurried pulse holding the vocal cord extension across 6 finger movements

assessment_bank.question: In 'فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ', what rule connects 'فِي' and 'أَنْفُسِكُمْ'?
What distinguishes Madd Lazim from all other secondary Madds?
options: Its duration is permanently and rigidly fixed at 6 counts without variation

assessment_bank.question: If a student confuses Madd Munfasil with Madd Muttasil, what is the core correction?
options: Point out word boundaries: Muttasil is inside one word; Munfasil spans across two words

assessment_bank.question: In 'تُبُوءُوا بِإِثْمِكُمْ', how many Madd rules are triggered?
options: Multiple (Tabii in tubuuu, Munfasil in uu-bi-ithmikum)

assessment_bank.question: What is the acoustic effect of Madd Lazim Kalimi Thaqil?
options: A majestic 6-count elongation crashing into a heavy, doubled consonant sound with Shaddah

assessment_bank.question: How should an AI evaluation engine score a student who lengthens Madd Munfasil to 6 counts?
options: Acceptable depending on transmission route, but flag if deviating from standard Hafs 4-5 count tempo

assessment_bank.question: Which Madd type represents the absolute longest required duration in standard Tajweed?
In 'صَاقَّة' or similar heavy constructs, what governs the length?
Summarize the core definitions of Madd Munfasil and Madd Lazim:
options: Munfasil is 4-5 counts across two words when Madd meets Hamzah; Lazim is strictly 6 counts when Madd meets permanent Sukoon or Shaddah
